text:
jenny: security-bot flagged a suspicious exec from an initContainer on node ip-10-3-45-12. initContainer had CAP_NET_ADMIN and a host mount. outbound connection to an unfamiliar IP was observed. :eyes:
security-bot: alert details: pod=cni-init-bootstrap-7f4c ns=kube-system image=ghcr.io/internal/cni-bootstrap:v1.2.3 digest=sha256:abc123def... command=sh -c 'curl http://3.120.45.67/p/register' env=AWS_REGION=us-west-2
raj: on it — pulling the pod yaml now. someone run: `kubectl get pod cni-init-bootstrap-7f4c -n kube-system -o yaml > /tmp/cni.yaml` and share
mike: ran `kubectl logs -n kube-system cni-init-bootstrap-7f4c -c init | tail -n50` — shows `aws kms:Decrypt success` followed by a write to `/hostfs/etc/hosts`. suspicious
elaine: that KMS decrypt line is odd. who/what principal called kms:Decrypt? check CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt events for alias/ri-prod-cmk around 18:32 UTC
sre-oncall: cordoning node ip-10-3-45-12 now: `kubectl cordon ip-10-3-45-12`. evicting non-critical pods. adding taint: `kubectl taint nodes ip-10-3-45-12 security=quarantine:NoSchedule`
opsbot: deployment automation log: daemonset cni-manager restarted at 18:30 by deploy-bot (user: infra-ci). rollback triggered to previous image per policy
raj: noticed a RoleBinding created ~3 minutes before pod launch: `kubectl get rolebinding -n kube-system | grep cni-bootstrap-controller` -> created by user `svc-account:infra-deploy`. that SA should not have cluster-admin
jenny: audit logs show an API server `create rolebinding` action by a token issued to infra-deploy SA via OIDC refresh — possible leaked CI token on runner
mike: containment checklist: 1) cordon + taint node (done) 2) delete suspicious pod (done) 3) rotate infra-deploy SA token and remove cluster-wide perms 4) revoke any KMS grants that were created
elaine: filed KMS revoke request for grants tied to role `infra-deploy` (ticket KMS-472). also flagged key for rotation window. copying kms-admins
security-bot: running cluster-wide image-scan for images used in last 7 days. initial prioritization: images with changed digest vs registry record and network binaries first
raj: opening P1 incident, pinging legal and infra leads. starting forensic capture of node (snapshot + disk) — `gcloud compute instances export` queued
jenny: draft incident blurb (for #incidents after approvals): "We detected a suspicious initContainer in kube-system which attempted outbound connections and performed KMS operations. Node quarantined, pod removed, investigation underway. No customer data impact identified so far." will post once legal signs off
mike: post-mortem action items: - deny hostNetwork/hostPID for initContainers in kube-system via admission control - enforce RBAC least-privilege for infra-deploy SA - require KMS grants to have IAM conditions limiting VPC/SourceIPs - prevent CI from having long-lived credentials
elaine: quick mitigation applied: OPA gate added to deny initContainers with host mounts in kube-system, PR #438 created
sre-oncall: monitoring: added CloudTrail -> slack subscription for kms:Decrypt on ri-prod-cmk. alert threshold set to 1 decrypt/minute for that key
opsbot: uploaded /var/log/pods, image layers, and node snapshot to secure bucket `ri-forensics-2026-03-20` (restricted access)
jenny: thanks everyone — keep replies here for coordination. scheduling tabletop + post-incident review tomorrow 10:00 PST. :white_check_mark:
